text:
Under a pale light

Life runs, dances, and writhes,

Impure and shrill.

As soon as to the heavens


Joyous night ascends

And everything, even hunger, calms,

Hiding shame,

The Poet says to himself: "At last!


My vertebrae, like my soul,

Covet sweet repose;

Full of funereal dreams


I will lean back

And roll among your veils,

Oh refreshing darkness!"

translation.title: The End of the Day
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's relief at nightfall, when noisy life gives way to dark repose.
